findings.reason: The protected Python solution partitions nums into independent remainder groups based on value % k. Within each sorted group, it uses dynamic programming with two states (skip and take) to count valid non-adjacent selections where adjacent means val - prev == k. The product of valid selections across all groups yields the total count of k-free subsets. The algorithm runs in O(n log n) time and O(n) space; no candidate is required.

Since elements differing by k must share the same remainder modulo k, partitioning by value % k decomposes conflicts into independent chains. Sorting each group and tracking skip/take states correctly enforces that no two chosen elements differ by k.

Grouping and sorting n elements takes O(n log n) total time. Scanning group elements for DP state transitions takes O(n) time. Total time complexity is O(n log n) with O(n) space for remainder groups. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts nums array and integer k, returning total count of k-free subsets including the empty subset.

The approach accurately details remainder modulo k grouping, sorted chain DP state transitions (skip, take), group result multiplication, and O(n log n) time / O(n) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover subset backtracking, global sorting with value maps, presence array counting, empty subset inclusion, zero conflicts, consecutive chains, and gap handling.
